# Register-ZbxActiveAgentHandler

## SYNOPSIS

Registers a scriptblock that answers an item key on a running active agent session.

## SYNTAX

### Direct (Default)

```
Register-ZbxActiveAgentHandler [-Name] <string> [-Key] <string> [-ScriptBlock] <ScriptBlock> [-PassThru] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Binding

```
Register-ZbxActiveAgentHandler [-Name] <string> [-Binding] <ZabbixAgentHandlerBinding> [-PassThru] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Register-ZbxActiveAgentHandler cmdlet adds a handler to the active agent session named in -Name: a scriptblock that answers -Key, run on the session's own runspace with the parsed key as its argument; its last output, as text, is the value the agent pushes for every active item with that key. A binding from New-ZbxAgentHandler can be piped in instead. It refuses a passive session; Register-ZbxAgentHandler takes either kind. It writes the session only with -PassThru.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Answer a custom active item

```powershell
Start-ZbxActiveAgent -Name 'web-agent' -Hostname 'web-01' -Server 'zabbix.example:10051'
Register-ZbxActiveAgentHandler -Name 'web-agent' -Key 'app.health' -ScriptBlock { 'ok' }
Test-ZbxAgentItem -Key 'app.health' -Session 'web-agent' | Select-Object Key, Value, IsSupported
Stop-ZbxActiveAgent -Name 'web-agent'
```

The scriptblock runs on the session's own runspace (module commands and your variables are not there); its last output, as text, is the value the agent pushes for app.health. Test-ZbxAgentItem -Session answers it locally.

### Example 2: Push a handler's value to the server

```powershell
Start-ZbxActiveAgent -Name 'web-agent' -Hostname 'web-01' -Server 'zabbix.example:10051'
Register-ZbxActiveAgentHandler -Name 'web-agent' -Key 'app.queue' -ScriptBlock {
    param($key)
    @{ orders = 12; mail = 0 }[$key.Parameters[0]]
}
Start-Sleep -Seconds 12
Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' | Where-Object Key -eq 'app.queue[orders]' | Select-Object Key, LastValue
Stop-ZbxActiveAgent -Name 'web-agent'
```

Register right after starting: a check that runs before the handler exists is sent as not supported, and the server shows the item unsupported until the next good value. The item's LastValue is what the server stored.

### Example 3: Register a catalogue of handlers through the pipeline

```powershell
Start-ZbxActiveAgent -Name 'web-agent' -Hostname 'web-01' -Server 'zabbix.example:10051'
@(
    New-ZbxAgentHandler -Key 'app.health' -ScriptBlock { 'ok' }
    New-ZbxAgentHandler -Key 'app.version' -ScriptBlock { '2.4.1' }
) | Register-ZbxActiveAgentHandler -Name 'web-agent'
'app.health', 'app.version' | Test-ZbxAgentItem -Session 'web-agent' | Select-Object Key, Value
Stop-ZbxActiveAgent -Name 'web-agent'
```

New-ZbxAgentHandler bindings bind to -Binding from the pipeline, so one catalogue serves several sessions.

## INPUTS

- `string`: Bound to -Name (ByPropertyName). Text.
- `ZabbixAgentHandlerBinding`: Bound to -Binding (ByValue). One key/scriptblock binding built by New-ZbxAgentHandler, for piping into the Register-Zbx*AgentHandler commands.

## OUTPUTS

- `ZabbixAgentSession`: Represents an active or passive agent kept running as a session in the runspace.
